passages.text: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ for the faith of God’s elect and their knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness, in the hope of eternal life, which God, who cannot lie, promised before time began.
passages.sermon:
Paul serves God.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
God chose certain people.
Paul works for their faith.
Paul helps them know the truth.
This truth leads to godliness.
God gives hope for eternal life.
God cannot lie.
God promised eternal life before time began.
passages.original: Παῦλος δοῦλος Θεοῦ ἀπόστολος δὲ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ κατὰ πίστιν ἐκλεκτῶν Θεοῦ καὶ ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας τῆς κατ’ εὐσέβειαν ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι ζωῆς αἰωνίου ἣν ἐπηγγείλατο ὁ ἀψευδὴς Θεὸς πρὸ χρόνων αἰωνίων

passages.text: In His own time He has made His word evident in the proclamation entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior.
passages.sermon:
God is our Savior.
God gave me a command.
God entrusted me with a proclamation.
God made His word clear through this proclamation.
God chose the right time to reveal His word.
passages.original: ἐφανέρωσεν δὲ καιροῖς ἰδίοις τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ ἐν κηρύγματι ὃ ἐπιστεύθην ἐγὼ κατ’ ἐπιταγὴν τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Θεοῦ

passages.text: To Titus, my true child in our common faith: Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter to Titus.
Titus is Paul’s true child in their shared faith.
Paul greets Titus.
Paul asks for grace for Titus.
Paul asks for peace for Titus.
Grace and peace come from God the Father.
Grace and peace come from Christ Jesus.
Christ Jesus is our Savior.
passages.original: Τίτῳ γνησίῳ τέκνῳ κατὰ κοινὴν πίστιν Χάρις καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν

passages.text: The reason I left you in Crete was that you would set in order what was unfinished and appoint elders in every town, as I directed you.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to Titus.
Paul left Titus in Crete.
Paul had a reason for leaving Titus there.
Titus needed to set in order what was unfinished.
Titus needed to appoint elders in every town.
Paul had directed Titus to do these things.
passages.original: Τούτου χάριν ἀπέλιπόν σε ἐν Κρήτῃ ἵνα τὰ λείποντα ἐπιδιορθώσῃ καὶ καταστήσῃς κατὰ πόλιν πρεσβυτέρους ὡς ἐγώ σοι διεταξάμην

passages.text: An elder must be blameless, the husband of but one wife, having children who are believers and who are not open to accusation of indiscretion or insubordination.
passages.sermon:
An elder must be blameless.
He must be the husband of only one wife.
He must have children who are believers.
His children must not be accused of reckless living.
His children must not be accused of being disobedient.
passages.original: εἴ τίς ἐστιν ἀνέγκλητος μιᾶς γυναικὸς ἀνήρ τέκνα ἔχων πιστά μὴ ἐν κατηγορίᾳ ἀσωτίας ἢ ἀνυπότακτα

passages.text: As God’s steward, an overseer must be above reproach—not self-absorbed, not quick-tempered, not given to drunkenness, not violent, not greedy for money.
passages.sermon:
An overseer serves as God’s steward.
An overseer must be above reproach.
An overseer must not be self-absorbed.
An overseer must not be quick-tempered.
An overseer must not be given to drunkenness.
An overseer must not be violent.
An overseer must not be greedy for money.
passages.original: Δεῖ γὰρ τὸν ἐπίσκοπον ἀνέγκλητον εἶναι ὡς Θεοῦ οἰκονόμον μὴ αὐθάδη μὴ ὀργίλον μὴ πάροινον μὴ πλήκτην μὴ αἰσχροκερδῆ

passages.text: Instead, he must be hospitable, a lover of good, self-controlled, upright, holy, and disciplined.
passages.sermon:
An overseer must be hospitable.
He must love what is good.
He must be self-controlled.
He must be upright.
He must be holy.
He must be disciplined.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ φιλόξενον φιλάγαθον σώφρονα δίκαιον ὅσιον ἐγκρατῆ

passages.text: He must hold firmly to the faithful word as it was taught, so that he can encourage others by sound teaching and refute those who contradict it.
passages.sermon:
An overseer is God’s steward.
He must hold firmly to the faithful word.
He must keep the word as it was taught.
He must do this so he can encourage others.
He must use sound teaching to encourage them.
He must also refute those who contradict the truth.
passages.original: ἀντεχόμενον τοῦ κατὰ τὴν διδαχὴν πιστοῦ λόγου ἵνα δυνατὸς ᾖ καὶ παρακαλεῖν ἐν τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ τῇ ὑγιαινούσῃ καὶ τοὺς ἀντιλέγοντας ἐλέγχειν

passages.text: For many are rebellious and full of empty talk and deception, especially those of the circumcision, who must be silenced. For the sake of dishonorable gain, they undermine entire households and teach things they should not.
passages.sermon:
Many people are rebellious.
Many people speak empty words.
Many people deceive others.
Many of these people belong to the group called "the circumcision."
We must silence these people.
They teach things they should not teach.
They do this for shameful profit.
They destroy entire households.
passages.original: Εἰσὶν γὰρ πολλοὶ καὶ ἀνυπότακτοι ματαιολόγοι καὶ φρεναπάται μάλιστα οἱ ἐκ τῆς περιτομῆς οὓς δεῖ ἐπιστομίζειν οἵτινες ὅλους οἴκους ἀνατρέπουσιν διδάσκοντες ἃ μὴ δεῖ αἰσχροῦ κέρδους χάριν

passages.text: As one of their own prophets has said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons.”
passages.sermon:
A prophet from among the Cretans spoke about his own people.
He said, “Cretans are always liars.”
He said, “Cretans are evil beasts.”
He said, “Cretans are lazy gluttons.”
passages.original: εἶπέν τις ἐξ αὐτῶν ἴδιος αὐτῶν προφήτης Κρῆτες ἀεὶ ψεῦσται κακὰ θηρία γαστέρες ἀργαί

passages.text: This testimony is true. Therefore rebuke them sternly, so that they will be sound in the faith and will pay no attention to Jewish myths or to the commands of men who have rejected the truth.
passages.sermon:
This testimony is true.
You must rebuke these people sharply.
This will help them become strong in the faith.
They must stop listening to Jewish myths.
They must not follow the commands of people who turn away from the truth.
passages.original: Ἡ μαρτυρία αὕτη ἐστὶν ἀληθής δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν ἔλεγχε αὐτοὺς ἀποτόμως ἵνα ὑγιαίνωσιν ἐν τῇ πίστει μὴ προσέχοντες Ἰουδαϊκοῖς μύθοις καὶ ἐντολαῖς ἀνθρώπων ἀποστρεφομένων τὴν ἀλήθειαν

passages.text: To the pure, all things are pure; but to the defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure. Indeed, both their minds and their consciences are defiled.
passages.sermon:
Pure people see all things as pure.
Defiled people do not see anything as pure.
Unbelieving people do not see anything as pure.
Defiled people have defiled minds.
Defiled people have defiled consciences.
passages.original: Πάντα καθαρὰ τοῖς καθαροῖς τοῖς δὲ μεμιαμμένοις καὶ ἀπίστοις οὐδὲν καθαρόν ἀλλὰ μεμίανται αὐτῶν καὶ ὁ νοῦς καὶ ἡ συνείδησις

passages.text: They profess to know God, but by their actions they deny Him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good deed.
passages.sermon:
Some people claim to know God.
Their actions do not match their words.
Their deeds deny God.
These people are detestable.
They do not obey.
They cannot do any good work.
passages.original: Θεὸν ὁμολογοῦσιν εἰδέναι τοῖς δὲ ἔργοις ἀρνοῦνται βδελυκτοὶ ὄντες καὶ ἀπειθεῖς καὶ πρὸς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἀδόκιμοι
